target_customer: Developers and software companies that need to read employee and payroll data from systems such as Workday, ADP and Paylocity
problem: Connecting to each HR and payroll platform separately takes years of integration and business development work. NewCraft offered one universal API with test environments and documentation.
business_model: Subscription API, reportedly a monthly fee per employee (one profile; unverified)
product_category: Unified HR and payroll data API

founders.name: Cameron Sadler
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as sole founder with no background.

technical_complexity.rationale: Normalizing many HR systems, several without public APIs, is laborious and fragile engineering rather than research. A two person team had to cover a long list of vendors.

defensibility.rationale: Once customers integrate, switching costs exist, but each connector was reproducible and rivals could build the same unified layer.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: ADP released a public API program and later unified API vendors emerged. Paylocity bought an integration platform (Cloudsnap) at a later date. No source shows what happened to NewCraft itself.

market_need_then: The YC description cites companies spending over 10 million dollars and years on integrations to reach employee systems. No independent 2018 demand data was found.

branding.domain_note: newcraft.io, not a .com, which now returns 404.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community material about the brand was found, and the name is generic.

outcome_analysis: NewCraft was a two person YC W18 team building a universal HR and payroll API. The YC page lists it as acquired but no press release, acquirer or date was found, and no priced funding round was verified. The cause or terms of the exit are not public, so no success or failure factors are asserted.
notes: Unverified: aggregators report about 120 thousand dollars raised, a seed dated 2018-08-24 (CB Insights) or 2018-03-19 with Precursor Ventures and Sinai Capital Partners (Bounce Watch), and one listing says acquired by Modern Health. These conflict and are not recorded as rounds or an acquirer. Company site newcraft.io returned 404. A dated 2018 competitor search returned only 2026 comparisons, so the list is empty. Update: two seed rounds are recorded, each from a single database (CB Insights 120K on 2018-08-24; Bounce Watch 2018-03-19 with no amount, which also lists a 120K YC round dated 2018-01-01, probably a placeholder). They may overlap. The Modern Health acquirer claim was not confirmed by a cross-check search and stays unrecorded.
